label: World Bank Procurement Notices
terms_note: World Bank open data API, keyless; terms of use = World Bank open data licence.

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes** for discovery (open-data search API) Confidence high (live API opened).

endpoints.notes: total, procnotices[]: id, notice_type, noticedate, notice_status, project_ctry_name, project_id, project_name, bid_reference_no, bid_description, deadline fields, url

reference.limits: - World Bank open-data terms; keyless; no limit on the page. - Bids go to the borrower's implementing agency named in the notice (assist). - World Bank open data API, keyless; terms of use = World Bank open data licence.

adapter.rate_note: Keyless open-data API; no rate limit is published. One request per second.
adapter.terms: World Bank open data terms; bids go to the borrower's implementing agency named in each notice.

search_postings.note: GET /api/v2/procnotices?format=json with the World Bank Search API conventions documented on the API page: qterm (full-text query), rows (page size, default 10) and os (0-based record offset). The procnotices collection itself has no dedicated reference page (confidence medium); fields are from the live response: id, notice_type, noticedate (DD-Mon-YYYY), notice_status, project_ctry_name, project_id, project_name, bid_reference_no, bid_description, procurement_method_name, submission_date, notice_text (HTML). total is a string in the response, so total is null. buyer is the financed project's name; contract awards are included (notice_type). Some notices carry no bid_description; their title falls back to project_name (live check 2026-09-26).

get_posting.note: Same collection filtered by id (e.g. OP00470638).

not_offered.me: No credentials to verify ('auth: none') and no account endpoint.
not_offered.submit_bid: Bids are submitted to the borrower's implementing agency as each notice instructs; the API is read-only.
not_offered.credits: No account or credit endpoint; the API is keyless.

live_check.notes: fixed: notices without bid_description had a null title (schema-invalid); title falls back to project_name. Result order is not stable upstream (identical requests return ties in different orders), so py/ts first ids can differ; all read tools answered, schema-valid, pagination advances
